title: Dysentery (bloody diarrhoea from infection)

items: Dysentery is diarrhoea with blood or mucus, caused by germs that invade the bowel wall.
Common causes include Shigella and amoeba.
Diarrhoea with blood or mucus, and belly cramps.
Tenesmus (a painful urge to pass stool with little coming out).
Fever, which is often high with bacterial causes.
Stool culture and stool microscopy, which are sent routinely.
Blood count and kidney function tests.
Your doctor will choose antibiotics based on the stool result.
Treatment depends on the germ found.

sections.h: What you can do at home
items: Wash hands well and do not prepare food for others while unwell.
Tell your doctor if the blood or diarrhoea does not settle.
This leaflet gives general information. Follow your doctor's advice.
